usageNotes: Use this to get a fleet-wide snapshot of firewall enablement across all PVE remotes registered in PDM — covering cluster-level, per-node, and per-guest (QEMU/LXC) status in a single call. The `status` field is optional on each object, meaning it may be absent if PDM cannot reach the remote or node at query time; always null-check before acting on enabled/active/all counts. Requires `Resource.Audit` privilege on each remote being queried.

examples.summary: Get firewall status across all PVE remotes

tips: A missing `status` field on a remote, node, or guest indicates PDM could not retrieve firewall data for that object — treat it as unknown, not disabled.
The `active` count reflects rules currently enforced by the kernel; `all` includes disabled rules. A gap between the two means some rules exist but are toggled off.
Cross-reference guests with `kind` (lxc vs qemu) to distinguish container vs VM firewall posture — they use different iptables chains in Proxmox.
This endpoint covers the PDM-managed PVE firewall layer only; standalone pfSense/OPNsense perimeter firewalls are out of scope.
